title_en: Wuhan Atlantic Continuous Casting Equipment Engineering Co., Ltd. v. Song Zuxing — dispute over company profit distribution
ruling_gist_en: In cases where civil and criminal proceedings overlap, facts determined in a criminal judgment generally have preclusive effect on subsequent civil litigation. However, factual findings of innocence in a prior criminal case require differentiation based on specific circumstances. A criminal judgment of acquittal does not necessarily lead to a conclusion that no tort or breach of contract exists in the civil case; whether the relevant conduct exists still needs to be determined and assessed in light of the evidence.

full_text_en:
Wuhan Atlantic Continuous Casting Equipment Engineering Co., Ltd. v. Song Zuxing — dispute over company surplus distribution

【Ruling Summary】

In cases involving the intersection of civil and criminal proceedings, facts found in a criminal judgment generally have a preclusive effect on subsequent civil litigation. However, where a prior criminal case finds a person not guilty, the determination of facts requires differentiation based on specific circumstances. A criminal judgment of not guilty does not necessarily lead to the conclusion in a civil case that no tortious or contractual breach has occurred. The existence of the relevant conduct must still be assessed and determined based on the evidence.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2019) Zui Gao Fa Min Zai No. 135

Reapplying Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Wuhan Atlantic Continuous Casting Equipment Engineering Co., Ltd. Address: No. 1, Jiangxing Road, Jianghan Economic Development Zone, Jianghan District, Wuhan City, Hubei Province.
Legal Representative: Xu Rukui, Executive Director of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Wang Hongxia, lawyer of Hubei Deweijunshang Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Xu Yang, lawyer of Grandall Law Firm (Beijing).

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Song Zuxing, male, born on May 4, 1966, Han ethnicity, residing in Wuhan City, Hubei Province.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Baojun, lawyer of Beijing Kangda Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Huo Jincheng, lawyer of Beijing Kangda Law Firm.

The Reapplying Applicant, Wuhan Atlantic Continuous Casting Equipment Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Atlantic Company), having disagreed with the civil judgment (2016) E Gao Min Zhong No. 1029 rendered by the High People's Court of Hubei Province in the case of dispute over company surplus distribution with the Respondent, Song Zuxing, applied to this Court for retrial. This Court rendered a civil ruling (2017) Zui Gao Fa Min Shen No. 2836 on December 21, 2018, granting the retrial of this case. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and held a hearing on June 18, 2019. Wang Hongxia and Xu Yang, agents ad litem of Atlantic Company, and Song Zuxing and his agents ad litem Zhang Baojun and Huo Jincheng appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case has now been concluded.

Atlantic Company applied for retrial on the following grounds: (A) Song Zuxing violated the non-competition agreement stipulated in the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement" by providing registered capital and technical support to Wuhan Hengruigu Metallurgical Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hengruigu Company); (B) Song Zuxing violated the confidentiality obligations stipulated in the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement" by retaining the trade secrets of Atlantic Company without authorization and providing them to Hengruigu Company for use; (C) Pursuant to the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement," Song Zuxing should be ordered to return the compensation and bonus payments and bear corresponding liability for breach of contract. In summary, Atlantic Company applied for retrial under Articles 200(1), (5), and (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, requesting: 1. to set aside the first and second instance judgments in this case; 2. to remand for retrial or amend the judgment to support Atlantic Company's claims; 3. to have Song Zuxing bear the litigation costs of this case.

Song Zuxing argued in defense: (A) According to the findings in the relevant criminal case, Song Zuxing had no connection with Hengruigu Company, and there was no violation of non-competition and confidentiality obligations; (B) Even if Song Zuxing had committed any breach of contract, as alleged by Atlantic Company, the liability for breach should be determined based on the specific circumstances of the breach; (C) The losses of Atlantic Company had already been sufficiently compensated in another case, and its related claims should not be upheld. In summary, Song Zuxing requested the dismissal of Atlantic Company's retrial application.

Atlantic Company filed a complaint with the court of first instance, alleging that Song Zuxing had violated the relevant provisions of the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement" signed with Atlantic Company, and that Atlantic Company was entitled to demand the return of the compensation and bonus payments already made, as well as liquidated damages amounting to 30% of the paid bonuses. It requested the court: 1. to order Song Zuxing to return the total bonus payments already received, amounting to RMB 10,514,462.44; 2. to order Song Zuxing to pay liquidated damages of RMB 3,154,338.73; 3. to order Song Zuxing to bear all litigation costs of this case.

The court of first instance found the following facts upon trial:

On September 29, 2010, Party A (Song Zuxing), Party B (Liu Lianqun, Liu Weiwei, Xiao Chaoying), and Party C (Atlantic Company) entered into a "Memorandum." The memorandum provided that Party A agreed to transfer to Party B, and Party B agreed to acquire from Party A, the 18% equity interest in Party C owned by Party A (hereinafter referred to as the target equity); Party A intended to no longer serve as a senior management officer of Party C and to terminate the employment relationship with Party C. On the same day, Song Zuxing and Atlantic Company signed the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement," under which Song Zuxing, having served as a senior management officer of Atlantic Company and having full knowledge of Atlantic Company's technical secrets and other trade secrets, undertook that upon leaving office, he would not engage in any conduct detrimental to the interests of Atlantic Company, including but not limited to: acts harming the reputation of Atlantic Company or its shareholders, senior management; acts violating confidentiality obligations; acts violating non-competition obligations; and other acts that might endanger the interests of Atlantic Company.

The parties also specified the scope of confidentiality obligations and the scope of technical secrets. Regarding non-competition, it was agreed that within two years from the date of Song Zuxing's departure, he would not assume any position in any other employer that produced or operated similar products or engaged in similar business as Atlantic Company, nor would he provide consulting or advisory services to similar business organizations. In consideration for Song Zuxing's fulfillment of the non-competition obligation, Atlantic Company agreed to pay Song Zuxing economic compensation totaling RMB 2.4 million, to be paid in monthly installments after Song Zuxing's departure, with the full amount to be paid upon the expiration of the two-year period. In addition to the economic compensation, Atlantic Company also agreed to give Song Zuxing additional bonuses totaling RMB 20.75 million in the manner agreed upon. The conditions for payment of the said bonuses were: Song Zuxing had completed all relevant transfer of items, financial, and work handover procedures as required by Atlantic Company; and Song Zuxing had fully performed all obligations under this agreement.

The parties also stipulated liability for breach of contract: if Song Zuxing failed to perform the non-competition obligation, or performed it not in accordance with the agreement, Atlantic Company could suspend payment of all economic compensation and bonuses under Articles 6 and 7 of this agreement, and was entitled to take appropriate countermeasures based on the specific circumstances of the breach.

The court of first instance also found: On January 4, 2016, the People's Procuratorate of Jiang'an District, Wuhan City, filed a public prosecution with the People's Court of Jiang'an District, Wuhan City, charging Hengruigu Company and Yang Yuxiang (former head of the Market Development Department of Atlantic Company, currently the legal representative of Hengruigu Company) with suspected infringement of trade secrets. The investigation revealed: Atlantic Company, established on October 17, 2001, was the first specialized technology company in China engaged in continuous casting technology research, development, and turnkey projects for continuous casting engineering. The company possessed advanced core technologies for continuous casting machines, and the relevant design drawings and design materials were the core trade secrets of Atlantic Company. Atlantic Company had implemented strict confidentiality measures, including access control systems, and had adopted a policy of splitting the components of the complete continuous casting machine and distributing design and manufacturing tasks separately. On May 28, 2008, Atlantic Company signed a "Labor Contract" and a "Confidentiality Agreement" with Yang Yuxiang. On December 13, 2010, Yang Yuxiang left Atlantic Company due to illness. On January 27, 2011, Yang Yuxiang, in violation of Atlantic Company's requirements on protecting trade secrets, established Hengruigu Company, which engaged in the same continuous casting technology research, development, and turnkey projects for continuous casting engineering, thereby obtaining economic benefits. The People's Procuratorate of Jiang'an District, Wuhan City, believed that Hengruigu Company and Yang Yuxiang, by violating the requirements of the right holder on protecting trade secrets, used the trade secrets they had obtained, causing significant losses to the right holder. Their conduct violated relevant criminal laws and should be investigated for criminal liability for infringement of trade secrets.

The court of first instance held:

In the criminal case where the People's Procuratorate of Jiang'an District, Wuhan City, charged Hengruigu Company and Yang Yuxiang with suspected infringement of trade secrets, the public security authorities concluded their investigation without implicating Song Zuxing, and no finding was made that Song Zuxing had infringed upon Atlantic Company's trade secrets. According to the results of the criminal investigation, the conduct of Hengruigu Company and Yang Yuxiang allegedly infringing trade secrets was unrelated to Song Zuxing. Atlantic Company's allegation lacked factual basis and was not supported by the court of first instance.

Pursuant to the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement" signed on September 29, 2010, Atlantic Company had paid Song Zuxing RMB 10,514,462.44 in accordance with the agreement. Its request for the return of such payments and for liquidated damages did not comply with the law or the agreement between the parties, and was not supported by the court of first instance.

In summary, the court of first instance rendered the following judgment: Atlantic Company's claims were dismissed. The litigation costs were to be borne by Atlantic Company.

Atlantic Company, dissatisfied with the first instance judgment, appealed to the court of second instance, requesting that the first instance judgment be set aside. The grounds included: 1. The first instance proceedings were procedurally illegal. The monies in question were paid based on the employment relationship, and pursuant to law, this should have been a matter for arbitration by a labor dispute arbitration committee; the court of first instance could not directly accept the case. Furthermore, this case should have awaited further investigation into Song Zuxing in the criminal case on infringement of trade secrets and the final judgment of the court. 2. The findings of fact by the court of first instance were seriously erroneous. Song Zuxing had violated the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement," and was not entitled to demand any payments from Atlantic Company under the agreement. Moreover, pursuant to the contractual terms, he should return the payments already made and pay liquidated damages and compensation for losses.

During the second instance, Atlantic Company submitted evidence related to its appeal, including:

Evidence 4: Record of inquiry of Zhang Ping, legal representative of Wuhan Huafei Continuous Casting Control Engineering Co., Ltd., conducted by the Economic Investigation Detachment of Wuhan Public Security Bureau on October 12, 2013.

Evidence 5: Three charts showing the flow of funds. Atlantic Company argued that, based on the capital flow chart for the establishment of Hengruigu Company, which was included in the criminal case files, every stage of the circulation of the RMB 10 million registered capital was under the control of Song Zuxing, and Song Zuxing's conduct had fully violated the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement."

Evidence 6, 7, and 8: Business registration information of Wuhan New Future Trading Co., Ltd., Hubei Ruheng Pawn Co., Ltd., and Wuhan Qidali Investment Management Co., Ltd. Atlantic Company argued that Song Zuxing was associated with these companies.

The court of second instance held that, because the evidence submitted by Atlantic Company was inconsistent with the facts corroborated by other evidence in this case and with the findings of the criminal indictment, and was mostly circumstantial evidence lacking a necessary connection with the disputed facts in this case, it could not achieve its stated purpose of proof and was therefore not admitted. The facts found by the court of second instance were consistent with those found by the court of first instance.

The court of second instance held:

Articles 6 and 7 of the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement" clearly stipulated the amount and timing of economic compensation and bonuses to be paid by Atlantic Company. Atlantic Company did not dispute the amount already paid. Song Zuxing's request for Atlantic Company to pay the remaining bonuses and late payment penalties in accordance with the contract had factual and legal basis.

Regarding the issue of whether Song Zuxing had violated the confidentiality and non-competition obligations under the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement," this involved the difference between criminal evidence and civil evidence in cases involving the intersection of criminal and civil proceedings. In addition to authenticity, legality, and relevance, civil evidence should also be susceptible to a presumption of admissibility. A comprehensive review and assessment should be conducted based on the degree of relevance of each piece of evidence to the facts of the case and the connections among the various pieces of evidence. The numerous pieces of evidence Atlantic Company adduced to prove Song Zuxing's breach originated from the criminal investigation files and unilateral expert conclusions, while the criminal indictment did not include any charges against Song Zuxing, nor were there any findings of fact that Song Zuxing had infringed upon Atlantic Company's trade secrets. During the second instance, Atlantic Company failed to provide sufficient evidence to prove that Song Zuxing had violated the non-competition obligation or infringed trade secrets. The records of inquiries, witness statements, informal emails, or flow of funds from the criminal investigation stage alone could not prove that Song Zuxing had established or was the actual controller of Hengruigu Company, that he had violated the agreement by establishing another company competing with Atlantic Company in the same industry, or that he had assumed a position or provided technical services in a similar company. Therefore, given that all the evidence adduced by Atlantic Company was circumstantial and could not form an exclusive chain of evidence, its ground of appeal was not supported.

In summary, the court of second instance rendered the following judgment: The appeal was dismissed, and the first instance judgment was affirmed. The litigation costs for the second instance were to be borne by Atlantic Company.

During the retrial review stage, Atlantic Company submitted four pieces of evidence to this Court, including:

Evidence 1: The criminal judgment (2016) E 0102 Xing Chu No. 17 rendered by the People's Court of Jiang'an District, Wuhan City, Hubei Province. Atlantic Company argued that this judgment was made after the conclusion of the second instance hearing in this case and should constitute new evidence.

Evidence 2: Inquiry record of "Chen Xiong" from the criminal case files of (2016) E 0102 Xing Chu No. 17.

Evidence 3: Inquiry record of "Zhu Shiju" from the criminal case files of (2016) E 0102 Xing Chu No. 17.

Evidence 4: Remote forensic examination record from the public security authorities in case (2016) E 0102 Xing Chu No. 17.

Atlantic Company claimed that Evidence 2 through 4 were evidence from the criminal case files that it could not have collected on its own during the original trial. Atlantic Company had repeatedly applied to the court of first instance and the court of second instance to obtain such evidence, but both courts failed to do so. It discovered these three pieces of evidence after the criminal judgment became final, and they should be considered new evidence under the law. Atlantic Company argued that, based on the criminal judgment (2016) E 0102 Xing Chu No. 17, the inquiry records of "Chen Xiong" and "Zhu Shiju" from the case files, the remote forensic examination record, and the witness statements of "Zhou Li" and "Fu Yu," it could be proven that Song Zuxing provided financial and technical support for Hengruigu Company's criminal infringement of trade secrets, seriously violating the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement."

Song Zuxing challenged the evidence, arguing that Evidence 1 through 4 did not constitute new evidence under Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law. Evidence 1 found that Hengruigu Company and Yang Yuxiang were guilty of infringing trade secrets, but did not implicate Song Zuxing. Evidence 2 through 4 were not evidence discovered after the second instance; Atlantic Company had previously submitted copies of criminal evidence from the court that accepted the criminal case. Therefore, Song Zuxing doubted the truthfulness of Atlantic Company's claim that it could not collect the above evidence on its own.

During the retrial hearing, Song Zuxing submitted two sets of evidence to this Court:

Evidence 1: Notarial certificate (2019) E Jiang Tian Nei Zheng Zi No. 1512, which recorded photographs of Yang Yuxiang attending a meeting as a representative of Atlantic Company in March 2019, and related meeting materials. This was used to prove that Yang Yuxiang, as a person affiliated with Atlantic Company, participated in relevant technical exchange activities and had a close relationship with Atlantic Company, creating a conflict of interest, and thus the credibility of his relevant statements was low.

Evidence 2: Interrogation record of Yang Yuxiang from the criminal case files of (2016) E 0102 Xing Chu No. 17. This was used to prove that during the investigation stage before June 2013, Yang Yuxiang had never stated that Song Zuxing was related to Hengruigu Company, which contradicted his later statements.

Atlantic Company argued that Evidence 1 was incomplete and its authenticity could not be confirmed, and that Evidence 2 was insufficient to achieve its stated purpose of proof and should not be admitted.

This Court, upon review, held that Evidence 1 through 4 submitted by Atlantic Company and Evidence 2 submitted by Song Zuxing originated from public security and judicial authorities and were relevant to ascertaining the nature of the relationship between Song Zuxing and Hengruigu Company. Therefore, this Court recognized their authenticity and relevance. Their purpose of proof would be assessed in conjunction with other facts. Evidence 1 submitted by Song Zuxing was issued by a notary public, and this Court recognized its authenticity. However, given that the events it sought to prove occurred much later than the time period in this case, and Atlantic Company did not acknowledge that Yang Yuxiang was its employee, this Court did not recognize its relevance or purpose of proof.

During the retrial, Atlantic Company submitted an application to this Court, requesting that this Court obtain the case files related to this case from the criminal case (2016) E 0102 Xing Chu No. 17 and investigate the relevant information of the email account A@126.com to confirm whether the account was owned or used by Li Yanshuang, spouse of Song Zuxing. Pursuant to this application, this Court retrieved and copied the relevant evidence materials involving Song Zuxing from the case files of (2016) E 0102 Xing Chu No. 17.

On November 28, 2018, this Court issued a "Notice to Assist in Investigation and Evidence Collection" to Guangzhou NetEase Computer System Co., Ltd., to investigate the registration information of the email account A@126.com. On December 21, 2018, Guangzhou NetEase Computer System Co., Ltd. replied, providing the mobile phone number and date of birth of the registered user of the said email account. During the hearing, Song Zuxing acknowledged that the mobile phone number and date of birth used to register the email account were consistent with the relevant information of his spouse Li Yanshuang, and admitted that the registrant and user of the email account A@126.com was his spouse Li Yanshuang.

During the hearing, this Court explained the source, process of collection, and content of the above evidence materials. Atlantic Company and Song Zuxing conducted cross-examination on the above evidence materials. Additionally, both parties acknowledged that Atlantic Company had established a Product Data Management system (hereinafter referred to as "PDM") database for computer design drawings and materials, which was encrypted and subject to output restrictions. Prior to his departure, Song Zuxing had applied for and received a decryption key for the PDM system. Furthermore, both parties acknowledged that the computers of Hengruigu Company seized by the public security authorities contained project design drawings used by Atlantic Company.

This Court, upon review, finds that the criminal judgment (2016) E 0102 Xing Chu No. 17 related to this case has become final. That judgment found that Hengruigu Company and Yang Yuxiang had infringed upon the trade secrets of Atlantic Company, constituting the crime of infringement of trade secrets.

This Court, upon retrial, holds that the issues in dispute in this case are: (A) Whether Song Zuxing violated the non-competition agreement in the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement"; (B) Whether Song Zuxing violated the confidentiality agreement in the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement"; (C) If Song Zuxing violated the aforementioned agreements, what legal liability should he bear.

(A) Whether Song Zuxing violated the non-competition agreement in the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement"

Pursuant to Article 5 of the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement," within two years from the date of Song Zuxing's departure, Song Zuxing was not to assume any position in any other employer that produced or operated similar products or engaged in similar business as Atlantic Company; was not to provide consulting or advisory services to similar business organizations; was not to incite or assist other employees of Atlantic Company to work for or provide services to similar business organizations; and was not to, alone or with others, establish another similar business organization to compete in the market.

Based on the facts found by the court of first instance, Song Zuxing left Atlantic Company on October 20, 2010, while Hengruigu Company was registered and established in January 2011. Its business scope included the same continuous casting technology research, development, and continuous casting engineering general contracting as Atlantic Company, thus constituting a competitor of Atlantic Company in the same industry. Therefore, determining whether Song Zuxing violated the non-compete agreement primarily involves determining the relationship between Song Zuxing and Hengruigu Company.

The court of first instance has already noted that whether Song Zuxing violated the non-compete and confidentiality obligations under the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement" involves the differences between criminal and civil evidence in criminal-civil overlapping cases. The criminal indictment did not involve charges against Song Zuxing, and the criminal judgment also did not address whether Song Zuxing infringed trade secrets. Song Zuxing accordingly argued that he did not violate the agreement. In this regard, this Court holds that Article 10, paragraph 1, item (6) of the *Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings* stipulates that the parties need not adduce evidence to prove basic facts that have been confirmed by a legally effective judgment of a people's court. Paragraph 2 of that article provides an exception where the parties have contrary evidence sufficient to overturn such facts. According to this provision, in principle, facts predetermined in a criminal proceeding have a preclusive effect on subsequent civil proceedings. This is because judicial uniformity requires that civil and criminal judgments be consistent in their findings on the same facts, and the standard of proof in criminal proceedings is higher than that in civil proceedings, so basic facts found in a prior criminal judgment have preclusive effect on subsequent civil proceedings.

However, the preclusive effect of facts predetermined in a prior criminal case is not unconditional. In addition to the prior judgment having become legally effective and the facts determined in the prior judgment being relevant to the facts in the subsequent case, the proof of the predetermined facts must have followed legal procedures. For a prior criminal case affecting a subsequent civil case, a finding of guilt naturally constitutes a preclusive fact; whereas a finding of innocence requires a distinction between whether it is because the defendant indeed did not participate in or commit the criminal act, or because the evidence was insufficient or the facts were unclear, and whether there is contrary evidence. If it is the former, it has preclusive effect; if it is the latter, different findings may arise due to the different standards of proof in civil and criminal proceedings. However, the particularity of the criminal case related to this case is that the criminal prosecution did not charge Song Zuxing, so the criminal judgment naturally could not involve whether Song Zuxing participated in the criminal act, whether he constituted the crime of infringing trade secrets, nor would it make a clear determination on whether Song Zuxing's conduct violated the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement." Therefore, the facts concerning whether Song Zuxing and Hengruigu Company were related, and the nature of that relationship were not addressed in the prior criminal proceeding, much less verified and determined through proper procedures. Hence, they do not constitute predetermined facts from the prior criminal case, and certainly cannot be directly used in the subsequent civil proceeding to conclude that Song Zuxing had no relationship with Hengruigu Company.

The relationship between Song Zuxing and Hengruigu Company still needs to be judged and determined in this case in conjunction with the evidence. This Court holds that the capital flow chart prepared by the public security authorities during the investigation stage in the criminal case file of (2016) E 0102 Xing Chu No. 17, which was obtained upon the application of Atlantic Company, although not used as evidence for the final determination in the related criminal case, is objective evidence. It provides an objective description of the flow of the registered capital of Hengruigu Company, and it can corroborate the fund flow records of Li Yanshuang's related accounts and the statements made by both parties during the trial regarding the source of Hengruigu Company's registered capital. Based on this, it can be determined that all 10 million yuan of registered capital of Hengruigu Company originated from companies closely related to Song Zuxing or his spouse, Li Yanshuang. The registered capital was transferred from Li Yanshuang's account to the account of her niece, Li Ye, then to Yang Yuxiang's name, and used to register Hengruigu Company. After the registration was completed, the funds were transferred back to Li Yanshuang's name through a circuitous route. Song Zuxing argued that the registered capital was a loan borrowed by Yang Yuxiang from Li Yanshuang's niece, Li Ye, and that he was unaware of it. Investigation revealed that Li Yanshuang's niece, Li Ye, was an ordinary employee of a certain company with no other substantial income sources or investment returns. Moreover, the flow of the registered capital showed that multiple sums of registered capital were merely transferred through bank accounts under Li Ye's name to be pooled under Yang Yuxiang's name for company registration, and then subsequently transferred back to Li Yanshuang's account. Song Zuxing's argument that Li Ye lent 10 million yuan in registered capital to Yang Yuxiang is inconsistent with common sense and reason, and this Court does not accept it.

Furthermore, according to the remote inspection record of the email box B@163.com used by Yang Yuxiang, conducted by the public security authorities, it contained materials named after "Song Zuxing" sent from the email account A@126.com, including a "share entrustment agreement" and other documents related to Hengruigu Company. Based on the facts established during the retrial stage of this Court regarding the registration and usage of the sending email account, it can be determined that the above materials were materials sent by Song Zuxing through his spouse, Li Yanshuang, to Yang Yuxiang for the purposes of registering and holding shares in Hengruigu Company.

Synthesizing the above evidence and facts, this Court holds that the existing evidence is sufficient to establish that Song Zuxing is the actual capital contributor of Hengruigu Company. Within two years after leaving his position, he covertly established, through concealment, Hengruigu Company, which competes with Atlantic Company in the same industry, thereby violating the non-compete agreement. The courts of first and second instance erred in their findings of the relevant facts, and this Court corrects those findings.

(2) Whether Song Zuxing violated the confidentiality agreement in the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement"

According to Article 2 of the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement," documents, materials, diagrams, notes, reports, letters, faxes, tapes, disks, instruments, and any other forms of carrier that record Atlantic Company's secret information and are held or kept by Song Zuxing due to the needs of his former position shall belong to Atlantic Company, regardless of whether such secret information has commercial value. ... Song Zuxing shall, upon leaving his position, return all property belonging to Atlantic Company, including all carriers containing Atlantic Company's secret information. ... Atlantic Company may, after copying or erasing the secret information on the original carriers, no longer require Song Zuxing to return the original carriers. ... Regardless of whether the original carriers are returned, Song Zuxing shall not retain copies, reproductions, and/or excerpts of the above secret information materials.

According to Article 108 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China*, if the evidence provided by the party bearing the burden of proof, upon review by the people's court and in conjunction with the relevant facts, makes it highly probable that the fact to be proved exists, the court shall find that fact exists. It should be noted that the "high probability" in the foregoing provision refers to a state of possibility, not a necessary nature. Whether a certain piece of evidence can achieve this standard of proof can be comprehensively assessed in conjunction with other evidence.

In this case, Atlantic Company applied to this Court to obtain the testimonies and inquiry records of its employees in the criminal investigation file of (2016) E 0102 Xing Chu No. 17, intending to prove that Song Zuxing did not fully return Atlantic Company's confidential materials and items, thereby violating his confidentiality obligation. In this regard, this Court holds that although the above evidentiary materials appear in the form of inquiry records, this does not change their essential nature as witness testimony. Since these evidentiary materials were verbal statements made by employees who have an interest in Atlantic Company during the criminal investigation process, and they were not subject to cross-examination in the prior criminal proceeding, they cannot be directly used as the basis for determining this case. Moreover, whether they can be used as evidence in this case depends on whether they meet the requirements of law and judicial interpretation for the category of witness testimony.

According to the *Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings*, if a party requests a witness to testify in court, it shall submit a written application to the people's court before the expiration of the time limit for adducing evidence. The people's court shall require the witness to testify in court and accept questions from the adjudicators and the parties. In this case, Atlantic Company did not apply for its employees to testify as witnesses in court. Furthermore, the witness testimony of its employees does not fall under the category of evidence that a party cannot collect on its own due to objective reasons as stipulated in the Civil Procedure Law. Therefore, the above evidentiary materials do not comply with legal provisions, and this Court does not admit them. However, based on the basic facts found in the legally effective judgment (2016) E 0102 Xing Chu No. 17, which determined that Hengruigu Company constituted the crime of infringing Atlantic Company's trade secrets, particularly the discovery of Atlantic Company's technical drawings at Hengruigu Company, combined with the determination in this case that Song Zuxing covertly contributed capital to establish Hengruigu Company, that he was the actual controller of Hengruigu Company, and that he violated the non-compete agreement, it can be inferred that the fact to be proved — that Song Zuxing's conduct also violated the confidentiality obligation under Article 2 of the aforementioned "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement" — exists with high probability. Therefore, this Court supports Atlantic Company's related claims. The courts of first and second instance erred in their findings of the relevant facts, and this Court corrects those findings.

Song Zuxing argued that since the related criminal case did not find him guilty of the crime of infringing trade secrets, his liability should not be determined in this case. In this regard, this Court holds that the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement" was concluded between Wuhan Atlantic Company and Song Zuxing based on their genuine intentions and does not violate the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations. Therefore, it is legally binding on both Wuhan Atlantic Company and Song Zuxing, and both parties shall perform their obligations in accordance with the agreement. At the same time, there are differences between the standard of proof in criminal cases and that in civil cases. Moreover, as previously stated, whether Song Zuxing constituted the crime of infringing trade secrets does not constitute a prejudicial fact from the prior judgment. Additionally, the evidence in this case is not entirely identical to that in the related criminal case. Therefore, Song Zuxing's related arguments cannot be sustained.

(3) What legal liability Song Zuxing should bear in the event of violating the aforementioned obligations.

According to Article 9 of the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement," if Song Zuxing fails to perform the non-compete obligation or performs it in a manner inconsistent with this agreement, Atlantic Company may: ... (2) Reduce the economic compensation and rewards, with the reduction amount to be determined by Atlantic Company based on the losses caused by the breach; (3) Refuse to pay the economic compensation and rewards, and may require Song Zuxing to return the economic compensation and rewards already paid; (4) Require Song Zuxing to pay liquidated damages equal to 30% of the total amount of economic compensation and rewards already paid. According to Article 10 of this agreement, if Song Zuxing violates the provisions of this agreement and engages in conduct detrimental to Atlantic Company's interests other than those specified in Article 1(3) of this agreement, Atlantic Company may: ... (2) Reduce the reward payment, with the reduction amount to be determined by Atlantic Company based on the losses caused by the breach; (3) Refuse to pay the reward payment, and may require Song Zuxing to return the reward payment already paid; (4) Require Song Zuxing to pay liquidated damages equal to 30% of the amount of reward payment already paid as specified in Article 7 of this agreement.

As previously stated, Song Zuxing's conduct violated the non-compete and confidentiality obligations under the "Post-Employment Obligations Agreement." His methods were relatively covert and his subjective intent was relatively malicious. Atlantic Company's request for the return of payments and the payment of liquidated damages in accordance with the agreement has a legal basis, and this Court supports it. In this case, both parties confirmed that Atlantic Company had paid Song Zuxing a total of RMB 10,514,462.44 in reward compensation. Therefore, Song Zuxing shall return this amount and pay liquidated damages equal to 30% of this amount, i.e., RMB 3,154,338.73, totaling RMB 13,668,801.17.

In summary, the grounds for Atlantic Company's retrial are established, and its retrial requests should be supported. Pursuant to Article 207, paragraph 1, and Article 170, paragraph 1, item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The civil judgment (2016) E Min Zhong No. 1029 of the Hubei High People's Court is reversed;
2. The civil judgment (2014) E Wuhan Zhong Min Shang Chu Zi No. 00185 of the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court, Hubei Province, is reversed;
3. Song Zuxing shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, pay to Wuhan Atlantic Continuous Casting Equipment Engineering Co., Ltd. the reward compensation to be returned and liquidated damages, totaling RMB 13,668,801.17.

If the monetary obligation is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance shall be paid double in accordance with the provisions of Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Court acceptance fee for first instance: RMB 103,813; court acceptance fee for second instance: RMB 103,813. Both shall be borne by Song Zuxing.

This judgment is final.
